items.q: The injury chain written for albuminuria runs: albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → ______ → fibrosis.
items.exp: Albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → TGF-β → fibrosis. (Book p744)

items.q: Microalbuminuria (moderately elevated albumin) spans urinary albumin of:
Moderately elevated urine albumin matters because it is a:
opts: Marker of vascular integrity with higher thrombosis (CVA, CAD) risk from endothelial injury
Marker of isolated lower urinary tract infection
Benign finding that needs no further evaluation
items.exp: Marker of vascular integrity; ↑ risk of thrombosis (CVA, CAD) d/t endothelial injury; requires further evaluation. (Book p744)

items.q: All of the following are listed tests for proteinuria EXCEPT:
items.exp: Tests: 24 hour urine protein; spot PCR; spot ACR; urine dipstick test. (Book p744)

items.q: The urine dipstick test turns positive only when proteinuria reaches roughly:
items.exp: Dipstick: qualitative; positive only when there is ↑ proteinuria (~800 mg); detects only albumin. (Book p744)

items.q: Fill up: Significant proteinuria in a non-pregnant adult is urine protein above ______ mg/day.
Which statement about the dipstick test for protein is TRUE?
opts: It detects only albumin and should be supplemented with PCR/ACR/24 hrs urine protein
It detects globulins better than albumin
It quantifies protein accurately in mg/day
It is positive at microalbuminuric levels
items.exp: Dipstick detects only albumin; should be supplemented with PCR/ACR/24 hrs urine protein. (Book p744)
